subject: general
question: Two poles of height 20 and 14 meters are joined at the top by a wire which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The length of the wire is:
solution:
**Given:**

Height of one pole = 20 m 

Height of another pole = 14 m 

Angle made by the top of the poles with the horizontal = 30° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9475315a233963c697103f440bcfd0832f903c3175456eb7a8c6e4efba2fa39a.png] 

In triangle AED, AE/AD = sin 30° 

⇒ 6/AD = 1/2 

⇒ AD = 12 m 

**∴ The length of the wire is 12 m. **
